classification_policy.AVAILABLE_NOW: A concrete value was present in the live bridge/runtime evidence captured on this installation.
classification_policy.DERIVABLE_NOW: A deterministic value can be computed from concrete fields captured now, without implementation changes.
classification_policy.MISSING: No current signal or value was observed, and no reliable derivation is available.
classification_policy.UNRELIABLE: Only partial, optional, free-text, self-reported, or ambiguous evidence exists.
classification_policy.REQUIRES_IMPLEMENTATION: Reliable benchmark capture needs a new neutral field, event, or adapter propagation path.
classification_policy.overall_status_rule: The top-level status is the conservative end-to-end benchmark classification; bridge, codex, and claude classify each observation surface separately.

codex.path: neutral MCP bridge -> real Codex adapter -> official Codex MCP runtime

claude.path: Codex manager -> neutral MCP bridge -> real Claude adapter -> Claude Code runtime
claude.independent_worker_finding: The Claude worker could not directly observe wrapper session, model, duration, token, cost, cancellation, timeout, crash, or resume metadata.

manager_setup_failure.cause: The first ephemeral Claude launcher was asserted as supervisor, so its adapter was registered under supervisor rather than claude.
manager_setup_failure.persistence: none; the ephemeral database was removed
manager_setup_failure.audit_significance: Manager-side setup retries before task creation are not counted by the current bridge.

metrics.source: Neither live event stream contains run_id; shared/protocol/src/ids.ts defines newRunId but no audited state/event uses it.
metrics.notes: A benchmark run cannot currently group multiple delegated tasks under one durable identity.

metrics.source: Codex task task_nsygpxkjxf and Claude task task_x662mdqp7g appear on every task-scoped event and deliverable.
metrics.notes: Stable and supervisor-visible.

metrics.source: attempt.started, attempt.handle_set, and attempt.ended expose the integer attempt within a task.
metrics.notes: There is no standalone attempt_id; use the composite task_id plus attempt number.

metrics.source: BridgeEvent.agent, Task.owner, TaskAttempt.agent, and Deliverable.agent were populated in both live runs.
metrics.notes: The creator/caller and delegate are distinguishable in delegation.requested and task ownership.

metrics.source: Live snapshots reported official-codex-cli-mcp and claude-adapter(claude-code-cli(claude)).
metrics.notes: This identifies adapter/runtime implementation, not the selected model.

metrics.source: Direct probes returned codex-cli 0.147.0 and 2.1.226 (Claude Code), both exit 0; Claude launcher stderr also reported 2.1.226.
metrics.notes: Versions are currently out-of-band and are not persisted in bridge events or snapshots.

metrics.source: Neither live event/result recorded a model. Claude independently reported that prompt-declared model text is unverifiable from the worker.
metrics.notes: No authoritative model or fallback/switch history is benchmark-visible.

metrics.source: Both task records contained a persisted 36-character handle; attempt.handle_set exposed only attempt and handle_length.
metrics.notes: Raw handles are deliberately redacted from this audit.

metrics.source: Both task records reached DONE; task.state_changed events recorded lifecycle transitions.
metrics.notes: Current state and terminal timestamps are persisted.

metrics.source: Both live deliverables and delegation.completed events reported COMPLETE.
metrics.notes: COMPLETE, PARTIAL, and FAILED are structured values.

metrics.source: Codex exposed verification.recorded plus the deliverable result; Claude exposed the result in its deliverable with claude --version exit 0.
metrics.notes: Claude did not emit a separate verification.recorded event in this run, but the persisted deliverable retained the result.

metrics.source: VerificationResult has passed and exit_code per command, but exact test-case totals are only available when a worker includes them in free text/output excerpts.
metrics.notes: Command-level check counts are derivable; framework-level passed/failed test totals are not a structured metric.

metrics.source: Both DelegationOutcome objects reported attempts: 1; task attempt numbers and attempt events were also present.
metrics.notes: This covers orchestrator attempts, not internal format repairs or manager setup retries.

metrics.source: No structured rework counter exists. Codex may expose a free-text repair status; Claude reported 2 turns, which is not equivalent to rework. The pre-task launcher retry was invisible to the event log.
metrics.notes: Define rework explicitly before benchmarking it.

metrics.source: Both deliverables contained changed_scope: []; deliverable.submitted repeated the field.
metrics.notes: This is worker-reported and should be compared with an external tree diff for write-sensitive benchmarks.

metrics.source: Task/deliverable records contained artifact ID lists; the registry stores name, kind, byte count, and SHA-256. Both probes correctly reported zero artifacts.
metrics.notes: Artifact content is retrievable separately; large content remains path-referenced.

metrics.source: DelegationOutcome.duration_ms was 18742 for Codex and 112305 for Claude; independent manager timers differed by 1 ms.
metrics.notes: Task created/completed and attempt started/ended timestamps provide a second derivation.

metrics.source: No separate model/runtime duration appeared in either event stream. Claude reported wrapper duration fields are outside the worker boundary, but no actual value reached the bridge.
metrics.notes: Wall time currently mixes orchestration, process startup, model work, and post-processing.

metrics.source: created_at, claimed_at, attempt.started, and first status timestamps are persisted in both live runs.
metrics.notes: This derives control-plane scheduling delay only; adapter semaphore/process queue delay has no explicit boundary.

metrics.source: The event stream records first status and handle persistence, but neither is defined as a useful result and no first-content timestamp exists.
metrics.notes: A benchmark needs an explicit useful-result event or semantic rule.

metrics.source: Codex reported duration_ms: 400 on its verification. Claude's claude --version verification omitted duration_ms.
metrics.notes: The field is optional and cannot currently support cross-runtime comparison.

metrics.source: No input-token value appeared in either live result/event. Claude stated wrapper usage metadata is outside the worker boundary but supplied no captured value.
metrics.notes: Adapter propagation and a neutral usage schema are required.

metrics.source: No output-token value appeared in either live result/event.
metrics.notes: Output bytes are not a reliable token substitute.

metrics.source: No cached-input counter appeared in actual bridge outputs.
metrics.notes: Do not infer cache use from repeated prompts or subscription behavior.

metrics.source: No cache-creation/write counter appeared in actual bridge outputs.
metrics.notes: Needs runtime-specific mapping into a neutral field.

metrics.source: No component exposed an actual total and the component token counters needed to derive it are absent.
metrics.notes: Do not estimate from text length in the controlled benchmark.

metrics.source: Claude status exposed only a 2-turn count; neither runtime exposed token values per turn.
metrics.notes: Requires turn-indexed usage records.

metrics.source: Execution handles are persisted, but no usage accumulator is associated with them.
metrics.notes: A raw handle must not become a telemetry key in exported reports; use an internal opaque correlation ID or digest.

metrics.source: No dollar value reached either bridge result. Claude mentioned a wrapper total_cost_usd field outside its view but produced no actual value.
metrics.notes: There is no auditable cost value for this benchmark run.

metrics.source: No plan or billing mode was inspected. Claude explicitly labelled its subscription inference weak; authentication/configuration was intentionally not read.
metrics.notes: Even a reported API-equivalent cost must be labelled estimated, billed, or unavailable.

metrics.source: Count delegation.requested or delegation.completed events. Each successful live database contained exactly one of each.
metrics.notes: The initial misconfigured Claude call created no task/event and is therefore not counted.

metrics.source: No parent task, parent delegation, or depth field exists in the actual request/events.
metrics.notes: Dependencies are not delegation parentage.

metrics.source: The bridge counts bounded delegation request/completion envelopes. It does not count internal model turns/messages; Claude exposed only the free-text fact that 2 turns finished.
metrics.notes: Report coordination envelopes separately from runtime conversation turns.

metrics.source: Task.blockers and task.blocked events are structured. The current persistent database had 4 blocker events; both audit tasks had zero.
metrics.notes: Blocker category and responsible actor are not structured.

metrics.source: Both live runs exposed lease acquire/release with no conflicts. The 113-event persistent sample contained zero lease.denied events, so the conflict shape was not runtime-proven here.
metrics.notes: The implementation defines lease.denied, but this audit does not promote an unobserved type to AVAILABLE_NOW.

metrics.source: The audited control plane acquires or denies leases; no wait interval or waiter lifecycle appeared in runtime evidence.
metrics.notes: Currently fail-fast rather than queued.

metrics.source: The persistent database had 11 idempotency records, but a replay returns the cached result without a replay event or counter.
metrics.notes: Stored unique keys cannot distinguish one call from multiple identical replays.

metrics.source: DelegationOutcome.attempts, Task.attempt, and attempt lifecycle events all reported one attempt for each live task.
metrics.notes: Manager calls that fail before task creation remain outside this count.

metrics.source: attempt.ended has a structured outcome; both actual attempts ended COMPLETE, yielding a directly observable failed-attempt count of zero.
metrics.notes: Failure detail quality depends on the outcome/error code supplied by the adapter path.

metrics.source: The certified tag records one successful resume per runtime, and handles are persisted, but no explicit resume.attempted/resume.succeeded event or counter exists.
metrics.notes: Comparing repeated handles across attempts is suggestive but not a complete counter.

metrics.source: No review event, review relation, or structured review counter appeared in schemas or live evidence.
metrics.notes: A task tag containing review would be convention, not reliable telemetry.

metrics.source: Human messages and manager corrections are outside the bridge event model; this audit's launcher correction was not recorded.
metrics.notes: Requires explicit supervisor intervention events and correlation to a run/task.

metrics.source: A blocker may contain a question in free text, but no question/request-for-human event exists.
metrics.notes: Do not count arbitrary question marks in summaries.

metrics.source: Blocked/unblocked timestamps can bound total blocked time, but blocker cause and resolution actor are not typed as human.
metrics.notes: A human_wait reason/category and resolved_at event are needed.

metrics.source: Neither live task nor the 113-event persistent sample contained human-input lifecycle events.
metrics.notes: Current answer is no.

metrics.source: Task specs are stored, but the final adapter-built prompt/context and its byte/token size are not persisted in either live run.
metrics.notes: Store sizes and digests, not raw private prompts.

metrics.source: delegation.requested.input_artifacts and TaskInvocation inputs are explicit. Both live probes recorded an empty list.
metrics.notes: Reference counts and artifact byte totals are derivable when artifacts are present.

metrics.source: Artifact hashes can identify repeated artifacts, but prompt/context segments have no digest or repetition accounting.
metrics.notes: A privacy-preserving context-segment digest is needed.

metrics.source: Both actual delegation envelopes contained only bounded TaskSpec data and input_artifacts: []; the Codex prompt contract explicitly says not to return chat history.
metrics.notes: Observed value for both audit runs: false. Session continuation may retain runtime-local history, but the bridge did not transfer manager chat history.

metrics.source: Input artifact IDs are resolved by the control plane and supplied to the adapter; both actual tasks used zero shared artifacts.
metrics.notes: The IDs are observable; retrieved byte/token volume is not.

metrics.source: Verification subprocess exit codes and outer audit command exit 0 were observed, but successful Codex/Claude model-process exit codes are not persisted as attempt telemetry.
metrics.notes: Transport failures may include an error code, but success lacks a symmetric structured process outcome.

metrics.source: No cancellation occurred in the live runs. Task CANCELLED and abort paths exist, but no actual cancellation event/result was captured.
metrics.notes: Needs a runtime cancellation reason/source field for benchmark use.

metrics.source: Both runs completed before their deadlines. Timeout error paths exist, but this installation produced no actual timeout event during the audit.
metrics.notes: A future timeout can surface as an error, but duration and killed-process evidence are not a dedicated record.

metrics.source: No runtime crash occurred. Adapter failures can become failed attempts, but crash vs transport/protocol/parse failure is not typed in current evidence.
metrics.notes: Add normalized termination_kind and raw exit/signal fields.

metrics.source: Both audit tasks persisted handles; the bridge-v0.1.0-certified annotation records successful Codex restart-resume and Claude semantic resume on this installation.
metrics.notes: The capability is proven, but automatic resume counts remain unreliable without explicit resume events.

metrics.source: An external Windows process census after both MCP clients closed found zero matching bridge runtime children; the bridge event/state does not store this.
metrics.notes: Requires an OS-level supervisor check; it is not self-reported by the bridge.
